diffs.diff: pin count: part has 21 (GND 3V3 SDA SCL INT INT2 P0 P1 GND2 GND3 P2 P3 3V3_2 3V3_3 P4 P5 GND4 GND5 P6 P7 3V3_4), datasheet reading has 13 (GND 3V3 SDA SCL INT 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7)
diffs.evidence: SparkFun Qwiic GPIO (DEV-17047) Eagle schematic net/pinref list: J9 (PTH row) 1=GND 2=3.3V 3=SDA 4=SCL; J7-1=!INT; J5: 1=!INT 2=P0 3=P1 4=GND; J8: 1=GND 2=P2 3=P3 4=3.3V; J1: 1=3.3V 2=P4 3=P5 4=GND; J6: 1=GND 2=P6 3=P7 4=3.3V (J2/J4 are the Qwiic connectors). That is 4 + 1 + 4x4 = 21 physical connection points, exactly the model's 21 pins in the same order. The second reading lists only the 13 unique signals (GND, 3V3, SDA, SCL, INT, 0-7); the model's extra pins INT2, GND2-GND5, 3V3_2-3V3_4 are the real duplicate terminals on the latch blocks, on the same nets. Same board, no pin is wrong.
